title: `TRY_CAST` and `TRY(…)`: which errors become NULL
verdict: `TRY` nulls invalid-input, out-of-range and conversion errors row by row; `TRY_CAST` nulls conversion failures, except casts of extension types
description: `TRY_CAST` returns NULL where the cast fails, and the cast page says it never raises. The planner's `CastCanThrow` qualifies this at v2.0.0: a cast to or from an aliased type (one an extension implements, such as `JSON`) can raise even as `TRY_CAST`, for example JSON to a MAP whose key fails to cast.

`TRY(expr)` turns errors caused by a row into NULL for that row (docs: `TRY('abc'::INTEGER)`, `TRY(1 // 0)`). It cannot wrap a volatile function, an aggregate or a scalar subquery; that is refused at bind time. In the executor it runs the child on the whole vector; on an error of type `INVALID_INPUT`, `OUT_OF_RANGE` or `CONVERSION` it runs it again row by row and gives NULL for each row that raises; other error types propagate (`Exception::IsExecutionError`). So `TRY(error('x'))`, an invalid-input error, also gives NULL, and an internal or out-of-memory error still raises.

Leads: which exception type each raising function throws (division by zero, overflow, domain errors), and DuckDB's tests of TRY (on main: test/sql/error/test_try_in_clause.test, test/sql/subquery/scalar/test_try_subquery.test; paths at v2.0.0 to check).
reference: Substrait's cast has `failure_behavior: RETURN_NULL`; the reference honours it on DuckDB for a double to an integer and an integer to a narrower integer, and refuses `TRY_CAST` to a decimal, of a decimal to an integer and of strings (`docs/reference-semantics.md`, #58). Substrait has no `TRY` of a general expression.
